title: Vector vs Raster Spatial Data
interviewAnswer: Vector data represents discrete geometry as points, lines and polygons; raster data represents space as a grid of cells. The correct representation depends on the phenomenon and operations.
why: Spatial representation determines storage, joins, visualization and modeling choices.
intuition: Roads and administrative boundaries are naturally vector; satellite imagery and elevation are naturally raster.
deepDive: Vector analysis uses geometry/topology; raster analysis uses aligned grids. Converting between them can lose detail or introduce resolution assumptions.
commonMistakes: Treating longitude/latitude as ordinary Euclidean x/y.
Assuming higher raster resolution always means higher information quality.
production: Choose formats/resolution based on query, model and scale.
workedExample: Store shops as points and land cover as raster, then aggregate nearby raster cells around each shop.

visual.title: Vector and raster representations
visual.caption: The representation changes which spatial operations are natural and efficient.
